transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (CTO, Synapse Health), Marcus Lee (Platform Eng), Rohit Sharma (Netops), Lena Ortiz (Security)

Auto-summary (auto): intermittent egress spikes observed during heavy inference bursts; canary kernel upgrade planned; need more telemetry from customer side.

00:00 Jordan: okay everyone, thanks for joining, 15:00 UTC, we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda — latency spikes, kernel upgrade risk, and follow ups, is that right?
00:18 Anika: yes that's right, thanks Jordan, we've got Marcus and Rohit to cover the logs, Lena for security ques.
00:35 Priya: hi, yeh, this is Priya, i'll walk through the perf numbers we ran overnight and propose a safe gate for the kernel/quant rollforward. disclaimer: some of these numbers are noisy because our canary was hitting the backlog.
00:50 Marcus: quick context, the spikes mostly show up between 08:30 and 09:10 PST when batch traffic hits the long tail, it's egress to the model nodes in the VPC, sometimes shows packet retransmits.
01:10 Rohit: and to add, we noticed a correlating SNMP counter jump on the peering router, but not always, that's weird. i have pcaps for the last two incidents.
01:28 Jordan: got it. Priya, can you walk us through the difference between the current kernel and the new quantized kernel you want to try? i.e. what are the failure modes?
01:45 Priya: sure, so current runtime uses the standard float kernel path — lower chance of arithmetic regressions but higher token latency. the quantized path uses int8 kernels and a different memory layout; risk is memory alignment edge-cases and slightly different token timing — we saw one case of kv cache thrash on earlier bench runs — spelled KV cash in the log sometimes, haha — anyway, that could show as jitter if not handled by the KV cache manager.
02:18 Anika: so does that explain the egress spike? we see network latency rise, not compute only.
02:30 Priya: it could be correlated. Hypothesis: quantized kernel changes request pacing and slightly increases burstiness which can blow out upstream buffers on the peering router, especially if MTU is mismatched or GRE tunnels fragment.
02:52 Marcus: ah about MTU — we discovered our corporate VPN uses 1400 MTU over GRE to the colo, but the model nodes expect 1500, we get defrag and reassembly, that spikes CPU on the routers.
03:10 Rohit: exact, that's the log i uploaded. look at ssh://shared-drive/pcaps/egress-20260609.pcap — you'll see retransmits at 08:37.
03:30 Jordan: good catch. So two tracks: infra side (MTU/tunnel) and runtime side (kernels/burst pacing). for runtime we can add a pacing shim and lower concurrent request window during canary.
03:50 Priya: yes, we can also bump the circuit-breaker threshold and enable prefix caching to reduce repeated prefix re-eval. But we need to measure end-to-end impact.
04:12 Anika: what does prefix caching look like operationally? storage of partial kv? any risk of data leakage?
04:30 Priya: prefix cache is local to the inference host's memory and is per-tenant; no external persistence. We honor KMS-encrypted keys and no customer data leaves the VPC control plane. Lena, correct me if i'm misstating the compliance posture.
04:48 Lena: that's roughly right. from a security POV we need the SOC2 artifact and the KMS integration doc. also need an architecture diagram showing where logs are retained.
05:05 Jordan: we'll share the SOC2 scope and KMS integration doc after the call — Jordan to Lena — action item.
05:20 Marcus: another datapoint — the peering device shows an asymmetric route sometimes which could increase RTT for some flows. might be BGP flap or secondary path.
05:35 Rohit: i captured path traces, sending those too.
05:44 Priya: thanks. for the canary plan i'm proposing: 1) do a controlled 8k-context bench (synthetic but uses real request shape) 2) enable quant kernel on 10% of traffic with pacing (2s ramp) 3) watch egress drop and packet metrics 4) rollback if retransmit > 1% or p99 increases by > 15%.
06:12 Anika: those thresholds seem reasonable, couple q's — how do we get metric visibility into packet drops? we only see VT telemetry at 1-minute gran but want sub-second.
06:30 Priya: we can forward tcpdump samples and enable per-flow counters on the peering device; also we've shipped a kprobe that surfaces kernel queue lengths from the inference host. for sub-second you need packet captures; Marcus/Rohit can trigger capture windows during the controlled runs.
07:00 Marcus: we can do that, but capturing at full rate is heavy. we'll do ring buffer captures for 2 minute windows.
07:15 Jordan: perfect. On the pricing side, Anika, i will send the updated dedicated-pool pricing with pilot uplift and a one-month overage clause.
07:32 Anika: thanks, would like the SLA for latency p99 to be in the addendum.
07:40 Jordan: yep will include p99 targets and canary safety rollback clauses.
07:48 Rohit: back to MTU, can redwood's runtime do MSS clamping or does that live in our edge?
07:58 Priya: MSS clamping is something we can add at the egress proxy in the host; we've done it for other customers but it'll need a minor config and a quick kernel module parameter change. low risk.
08:18 Marcus: any chance the fallback routing we saw last week (where it went to the hosted fallback) is tied to this behavior? we had a route policy that prefers hosted when latency > threshold.
08:36 Priya: yes that makes sense — the policy is latency-first; if the local VPC route p99 exceeds the threshold, requests flip to the hosted variant. that is intentional for availability but it's noisy metric-wise. we can tune the hysteresis.
08:58 Anika: okay so to summarize, we want: packet captures, an 8k bench, safe 10% canary with pacing and rollback triggers, and pricing addendum. anything else?
09:12 Lena: security asks: please include data retention window for logs, and confirm if any request bodies are persisted in plain text on S3.
09:28 Priya: we persist request logs for 30 days by default for pilot, request bodies are redacted unless you opt-in. we can shorten retention for you.
09:44 Jordan: i'll include a note about redaction and a contact for audit artifacts.
09:52 Rohit: i'll upload the pcaps and the traceroutes by EOD tomorrow.
10:02 Marcus: also want to trial lowering MTU on the colo router to 1400 across the path, run the bench, and compare. i'll coordinate changes with infra team.
10:18 Priya: good plan. Logging: we'll add an experiment flag to tag canary requests so you can filter them in your observability.
10:30 Anika: any known regressions with quantization we should watch for besides kv thrash?
10:40 Priya: there was a rare sequence alignment issue on an older model variant where tokens repeated — we patched that in the latest runtime but we'll monitor generation quality metrics as part of the bench.
10:58 Jordan: timeline / next sync? propose we reconvene after Priya's bench and after Marcus uploads pcaps. aim for next week Thurs 2026-06-18.
11:12 Anika: works for us.
11:20 Jordan: great. quick recap of owners and due dates now (verbal): Priya — bench by 06/18; Jordan — pricing and SOC2 doc by 06/14; Rohit — pcaps by 06/13; Lena — confirm SOC contact by 06/15; Marcus — schedule MTU test and ring captures.
11:45 Priya: i'll also attach the bench config and the rollback thresholds in the shared doc after the call (link: drive/synapse-pilot/bench-config).
12:00 Jordan: thanks all, closing notes: we'll try conservative canary and measure impact, don't hesitate to ping if you see anything during the night window.
12:12 Anika: thanks everyone. bye.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: drive/synapse-pilot/bench-config, ssh://shared-drive/pcaps/egress-20260609.pcap, SOC2 and KMS integration doc (will be shared).

Recap (auto): Controlled canary plan agreed with rollback thresholds; infra and security artifacts to be delivered; pricing addendum to follow.
